clue.text: Person out rambling

parts.note: reads as a hiker on a country walk, but 'out' means unconscious, asleep, while wandering about

explanation.surface: A walker heading off for a ramble in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' suggests outdoors, but here it means out cold, asleep; 'rambling' is wandering aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wanders about while still asleep is literally out of it and roaming, which is this somnambulist.

clue.text: Support South American volunteers at home

parts.note: US, short for United States, stands for American
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force of volunteer soldiers
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: Backing a group of US volunteers who are staying at home in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something up or bear its weight is a synonym of supporting it.

clue.text: Honour to be included in next Olympics

indicators.note: the answer is included within the run of letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: Hoping to receive an honour at the next Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone highly is to honour them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Invaluable and totally absurd!

definitions.meaning: beyond any price, worth too much to value

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling something both precious and utterly ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means without price, hence invaluable, and colloquially it also means hilariously absurd.

clue.text: Attention-seeker from area on border

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it

parts.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone seeking attention from a region along a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' places A above HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: This little cough is uttered to attract notice, so it is literally a seeker of attention.

clue.text: Attractive form of competition

definitions.meaning: informally, a stunningly good-looking person or thing
a tournament where losers are eliminated each round

explanation.surface: An appealing format for a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner is called this, and a cup tournament with elimination rounds has the same name.

clue.text: Stagger around parking and drive off

indicators.note: the word for stagger goes around the letter for parking

parts.note: to stagger is to reel
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone lurching around a car park before driving away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive off' looks like motoring away, but it means to fend off.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attacker is to force them back, a synonym for driving them off.

clue.text: Late shifts covering study course prepared this way?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, that is surround, the word for study
shifts means the letters of late are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: Late shifts at a restaurant kitchen where a course is being studied and prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late shifts' reads as evening work rotas, but 'shifts' is the anagram signal; 'course' is a pasta dish, not a study course.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta served with a little bite is cooked to the tooth, the Italian way a pasta course is prepared.

clue.text: String of words that could be fine in court?

definitions.text: that could be fine in court?
definitions.meaning: a penalty handed down by a judge, of which a fine is one example

explanation.surface: A phrase that might sound fine when spoken in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective meaning acceptable, but it is a monetary penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically it is a group of words; legally a fine is one kind of punishment a court imposes.

clue.text: Light altercation about sack

indicators.note: the word for altercation goes about, around, the word for sack

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or argument
to sack an employee is to fire them

explanation.surface: A minor quarrel over someone being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective modifying altercation, but it is the verb to ignite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to put a flame to it, the verb sense of light.

clue.text: Pretentious chap, note, expected back

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

indicators.note: the word for expected is read back, from right to left

parts.note: something due is expected

explanation.surface: A pompous man who left a note and is expected back.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an intellectual poser who affects learning or taste he lacks.

clue.text: Joint liability originally accepted by Delia for cooking

indicators.note: the first letter is taken into the rearranged name
cooking means the name Delia is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of liability

explanation.surface: A shared liability taken on by Delia, presumably the TV cook Delia Smith, for her cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges DELIA as ALIED, and 'accepted by' places L inside: AL-L-IED. Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint and this word both describe things joined or combined in partnership, as in a joint effort.

clue.text: Nakedly asked and revealed outline

indicators.note: nakedly means stripped of its outer layer, so the word asked loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: Someone asked bluntly and disclosed a rough plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nakedly' strips ASKED to SKE; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare framework or sketch plan, as in a skeleton of a story, is its outline.

clue.text: Colt perhaps backed to achieve gold

indicators.note: backed means the word for a firearm is read backwards

parts.note: Colt is a famous make of revolver, an example of a firearm
to get something is to achieve it

explanation.surface: A young horse, backed by a punter, winning gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' is the gun maker, not a young horse, and 'backed' reverses GUN to NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of the precious metal found in the ground is the classic example of a prospector's find.

clue.text: A log rewritten on China's twilight

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
rewritten means the letters of a log are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Ming was one of China's great dynasties

explanation.surface: A ship's log rewritten during dusk on a voyage to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China's' looks like the country but stands for its Ming dynasty; in a down entry 'on' puts the first piece above.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for dusk, the dim period after sunset.

clue.text: Annoying person one's put in shade

indicators.note: the letters for one's are put inside the word for shade

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: An irritating individual who is left in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' looks like shadow, but means a subtle gradation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest or bother can be a person as well as a thing.

clue.text: People won't work for such money

definitions.text: People won't work for such money

parts.words: People won't work for such money
parts.note: looks like a complaint about low wages, but describes money paid to workers while they refuse to work

explanation.surface: A complaint that wages are too poor to be worth working for.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pitiful wage; in fact it is money received precisely for not working, during industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Unions pay members an allowance during industrial action, so it is money earned by withholding labour.

clue.text: Heart's no different — it's this water

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the 's is counted as a letter of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentimental claim that one's heart is no different here by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges HEARTSNO; the 's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: This body of water lies between Britain and mainland Europe, so 'this water' is fair.

clue.text: Weapon that's Spooner's chief boast?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a boss is a chief
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A boast about the weapon belonging to a man named Spooner's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the starts of BOSS and CROW: B and CR trade places to give CROSS BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical bow mounted on a stock that fires bolts is a medieval weapon.

clue.text: Ample evidence of debts to support policeman

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes beneath the other

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Plenty of proof that a policeman has debts to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to support' means the debts piece sits beneath the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant or plentiful supply means the same as an ample one.

clue.text: Edicts from religious communities

definitions.meaning: monastic brotherhoods such as the Benedictines or Franciscans

explanation.surface: Decrees issued by monasteries and convents.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers official commands and monastic fraternities like the Dominicans.

clue.text: Slumps, beset by Chinese philosophy and maxims

indicators.note: the philosophy word is surrounded, beset, by the slumps word

parts.note: to slump is to sag
yin is the passive principle in Chinese philosophy, paired with yang

explanation.surface: A decline in fortunes surrounded by the wise words of Chinese thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' means surrounded: the slumps word goes round the philosophy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pithy statements of general truth, proverbs and adages, are maxims.

clue.text: Fruit's appearance in stone circle

indicators.note: the word for appearance sits in the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit
mien is someone's look or bearing
O has the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit spotted within a ring of standing stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone circle' suggests Stonehenge, but is two pieces, PIT and O. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet red pepper is botanically a fruit, often used to stuff olives.

clue.text: Cash invested in amateur, ostensibly

indicators.note: invested in means the answer is put away inside the following words

explanation.surface: Money put into an amateur venture, at least on the face of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' sounds financial, matching 'Cash', but signals a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of the eurozone is money, so the plural serves as cash.

clue.text: Thin fleece, navy on the outside

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's skin

indicators.note: on the outside picks just the outer letters of navy

explanation.surface: A thin fleece jacket with navy trim on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a jacket but is an animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Very slender or lean, as in skinny jeans, means thin.

clue.text: This girl — and not her mummy!

parts.note: nor means and not
ma is a childish word for mother

explanation.surface: Pointing out a girl and insisting she is not her mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so 'This girl' stands for a female forename.

clue.text: Cheese girl entering union with no end of speed

indicators.note: with no means the letter is removed

parts.note: a woman about to marry is entering the union of marriage

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of speed

explanation.surface: A girl rushing into marriage at reckless speed, with cheese thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl entering union' is a cryptic description of a woman marrying; 'with no' removes D, the 'end of' speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with a white rind named after its region of origin.

clue.text: Title-holder's depressing experience, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: A champion's dispiriting defeat, losing at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title-holder' suggests a champion but means someone holding legal title to property. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal title to property is held by its proprietor.

clue.text: Altercation with golf club recycling material

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A row breaks out involving a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal salvaged for reprocessing is material for recycling.

clue.text: Timorous people cry as cadets in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble signals that the letters of the fodder are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nervous recruits wailing when military cadets get into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish name for cowards, those who are fearful and easily frightened.
